\section{Reward-ranked strategy}

Reward is assessed qualitatively by four criteria: how early the target lies
in the Clay implication chain, how many later modules reuse it, how decisively
failure redirects the programme, and whether a finite certificate can probe
it before a long analytic investment.

\begin{longtable}{p{0.06\textwidth}p{0.32\textwidth}p{0.12\textwidth}p{0.36\textwidth}}
\toprule
Rank & Target & Reward tier & Reason\\
\midrule
\endhead
1 & Vacuum-weighted normalized multichannel one-step kernel & A+ & It is the
first open physical implication and composes H1, H4, H5, and H8.  Success
creates basin entry; failure identifies a missing state or normalization
mechanism.\\
2 & Exact coordinated-polymer spill scaling & A & New zero modes give a cheap,
decisive test of the repair backup.  An extensive lower bound would kill the
route; a boundary law would create a new constructive mechanism.\\
3 & Topology-complete retained state closed under blocking & A & H4 already
falsifies a tempting smaller state.  Closure is required before any
multichannel kernel can be iterated.\\
4 & Automated boundary-state sufficiency refinement & A-- & H8 can turn
counterexamples into a systematic retained-state discovery procedure and
prevent repeated history-erasure errors.\\
5 & Quantitative representation commuting-square calculus & B+ & It catches
orientation, chart, and limit-order defects but does not by itself provide
probability suppression.\\
6 & Atlas gluing and exceptional-set summability & B+ & Necessary for a full
measure, but best attacked after the normalized kernel and retained state are
frozen.\\
7 & Lyapunov-to-OS spectral theorem & B & High conceptual value and reusable,
but it lies downstream of the present physical bottleneck.\\
8 & Observable recovery/error-correction formulation & C & Potentially
unifying, but presently a toy analogy rather than a source of the missing
nonlinear estimate.\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\subsection{Primary mathematical target}

Let \(\Sigma_n\) be the retained state at scale \(n\), including continuous
collar data, center flux, orbit/cut information, and a compositionally
sufficient integer topological carrier.  Let
\(D_{n,\alpha}(\sigma,d\sigma')\) be the normalized bad-extension kernel for
channel \(\alpha\).  The highest-reward theorem is to construct positive
weights \(h_n\) and penalties \(\lambda_\alpha\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \sup_{\sigma\in\Sigma_n}\frac{1}{h_n(\sigma)}
 \sum_\alpha e^{\lambda_\alpha}
 \int_{\Sigma_{n+1}}h_{n+1}(\sigma')
 D_{n,\alpha}(\sigma,d\sigma')
 \le q<q_{\mathrm{crit}}.}
\end{equation}
The quantifiers must be uniform over positive-mass histories, finite volumes,
and cutoffs on the tuned trajectory.  The state weight must be constructed
without using the desired clustering or gap.

\subsection{Execution order}

\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
\item Freeze one \(\SU\) heat-kernel regulator, block, exposure order, and
positive-mass retained-history space.
\item Prove conditional sufficiency of the retained state.  Use refinement
counterexamples to expose missing center, continuous, orbit, or integer data.
\item Construct the exact normalized positive kernel and solve its finite
Perron problem.  Test whether the positive eigenweight behaves like a coarse
vacuum amplitude.
\item Prove the boundary-uniform continuous good-channel comparison, including
all normalizers and chart complements.
\item Prove charged numerator inequalities for center, cut/orbit, and full
integer topology channels.
\item Compose the kernel rows and verify a strict connected-set threshold.
\item Prove stability of the state space, weight, positivity, and constants
under one further block step before attempting indefinite iteration.
\item Only after repeated physical-unit contraction, transport a complete
observable core and invoke the conditional OS spectral theorem.
\end{enumerate}

The coordinated-polymer route remains a backup.  Its next decisive question
is whether the nonzero minimum-spill cost of a growing polymer is bounded by a
constant times its boundary.  If the cost remains extensive, the repair route
should be abandoned in favor of direct normalized integration.
